content.comment_body: Hi, I'm experiencing a similar issue with a recently purchased [product_name]. The Ethernet connection appears fine—green indicator and successful ping—but transfers are not working. The status message at the bottom looks like: *** date filename.lsc *** pc --> [product_name] but nothing transfers. If I use a [product_name] bought a month ago, everything works, but with a unit bought this week, transfer fails. I went to exchange the device at the shop, but the same problem persists. The firmware on the new unit is [version_no], which might cause compatibility issues? I'm using [product_name] [version_no]. Tried on both PC and Mac—same result. ---------------------------------------------------------------------- Split from [product_name] [article_no] connects but no transfer.

You are using the new [product_name] [article_no]. For this hardware with firmware [version_no], you need to update to [product_name] [version_no]. Update your software accordingly. You can perform the update via help > update-center or download the update file from the [company_name] website: [document], upgrades/updates, drivers

Thank you for your assistance. Now I understand why it doesn't work. Next, I need to address the upgrade process. I'm using a Mac running Yosemite 10.10.5. Please see the attached screenshot. Thanks [user_name] I also downloaded the file, but when I double-clicked on Setup, my Mac reported the file was broken. Tried manually with StuffIt Expander, but that didn't resolve it either.
Unfortunately, I'm unable to assist further. Only [company_name] Support can help here. Consider submitting a Support Request.
A Mac update is available on the [company_name] website, as mentioned earlier. You'll need to manually download the setup file yourself.

Thanks for the update. I tried again today, but received a message saying the file is broken and couldn't extract it with StuffIt. Ultimately, I managed to solve it using my old Asus from 2007. I find the communication from [company_name] unclear. There was no warning on the product packaging indicating that it requires [product_name] [version_no]. Initially, I thought the unit was defective and exchanged it at the store. This issue wasted a lot of time, and I only have a partial solution.
Indeed, this situation is quite frustrating. You should still consider submitting a Support Request, so you can see how [company_name] responds.

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced issues transferring programs to the latest [product_name] with updated firmware using [product_name] software. The transfers worked on previous models but failed on newly acquired devices. Attempting to update the software on MacOS led to broken file errors, resulting in confusion and considerable time lost. The lack of clear communication from [company_name] increased the frustration experienced by users.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect seamless project transfers to new hardware, along with clear compatibility information. They also anticipate that installing software updates should be straightforward and error-free across all supported operating systems.
